beta_new:
Start on the left flank of the small ledgy boulder; steady, sequential moves on big holds lead to a relaxing stretch.

Near the top bear a little right through a brownish band, then step over a small roof and reach the chains.

Work up a rock chute to a stance under a little roof; slot in protection, then launch across to the crack for some very good-feeling hand jams.

Stay focused on the thinner stretch near the top.
Mostly tracks a blunt arete, then breaks rightward at the very top to reach the anchors.

Work up to the small finger crack roughly fifteen feet up, clip, and shake out. Then shift right along crimps, deadpointing across to the crimp rail.

Fire off to a jug, continue up the wall to a pocketed section, make a few big moves and clip the chains.
Begin under the big hueco; pinch holds and deceptive sucker jugs lead to the anchors.
Start from a boulder, pull through a brief steep section up to bolt two, then follow the pocketed face up to the anchors.
Start at the rounded arete beside a big half-hueco, step rightward onto the slab, then go directly up the wall until the anchors.

Start up the chimney system to a belay ledge some 25 feet high, then keep chimneying past a bolt to a big ledge for the next belay.

From there, return up the gully and squeeze through a gap in the stone to a second chimney on the other side. Turn around to climb it onto a ledge beneath an arch.

Go west beneath the arch, then take the last chimney to the top.
Climb a short dihedral to clip the first bolt, then move onto the overhanging gray rock, where big dynamic reaches and a gorilla-swinging style pay off.
Aim for the piton on the face, which lies back below a huge roof, then cut rightward to a bolt and keep climbing the wall; solid nut placements show up along the way.
Head up to the roof, then traverse left and clip the anchors.
Start up the arete, then transfer to a hand crack and stay with it until a slab leads to the top; small cams are useful higher up.

moves.from: small cams are useful higher up

beta_new: Start on easy holds and pull over a little roof and onto thin ground. Work along edges for a while, then continue over a few bulges to the anchors.
Balance your way up the slab, which is thoroughly bolted, until you reach the anchors.
Four bolts lead onto a ledge system; above that, the headwall is steep and relentless. A 70 m rope will not reach the ground from the top, so use the mid-height anchor or find another way down.
Large jugs lead up to a blank face, where you step off the big footholds and a crimping sequence begins, ending with a tough last move before the anchors.
Climb the bouldery finger crack up onto a ledge, and then move across leftward to Muscle Shoals' anchors.
Walk up the wide lower part, then a brief offwidth layback and some chimney moves, with the occasional obstacle to surmount.
Sneak onto a ledge about ten feet off the ground, follow jugs up to a flake that faces left, and finish at the anchors.
Edges and pockets of good size dot a featured face, and a handful of moves are reachy; which line you take past the second bolt changes how hard it feels.

Reach to a solid hand jam in the roof crack, then swing your legs up high and into it. Shuffle outward until a flip around is possible, landing on a good stance under a bulge.

Mantle the bulge, then keep climbing wide crack to the top.

moves.from: very large cams, sizes 4.5 and 5, are needed

beta_new: Use the jugs and the concealed pockets scattered over the steep wall. The crux comes toward the top, after which jugs lead to the anchors.
Instead of moving left to the face, stay with the dihedral and layback through a thin section; easier climbing follows to bolted anchors.

Step onto a low boulder left of the arching corner, then get onto the rock from a low rail of jugs, usually covered in chalk. Follow the steep wall, crossing several bands of iron-rich rock, to a small roof and then the anchors above.
Near the top, move leftward to reach the anchors.
Begin standing atop a platform; a few hard moves take you to the first protection, which is high. The hand crack above is enjoyable and ends at gear already fixed inside the hueco.
Fight up the crack in the black dihedral until you reach the fixed gear.
Start off the boulder and climb pleasant terrain until a bizarre finish at the anchors.
Climb Dogleg's opening five bolts with their long moves, then veer left where Dogleg heads right; continuous long moves follow.
Figure out the opening sequence; easier slab climbing then leads to the anchors.
Veer leftward over the face, slotting gear into each of the three vertical gashes the route is named for. Then step across into a crack and follow it upward; one large move comes before the finish.
Hop over a little roof to gain the smooth arete and ride it until the protection forces a move off to the left. Bulges above need working out before the finish.
Stay with the crack, and when it peters out, shift to the right onto the steep wall and pull hard to a ledge, where you lower off.
Follow the crack up until it blends into the neighbouring route's upper bolts, then finish via an easy third-class gully or take the harder alternative direct.
Grab a lofty jug beneath the roof and crank across the lip to the face. After two bolts or so, work out to the left and fall-test your way upward.

Follow the left-hand crack as far as the roof, then shift to a corner and build a gear anchor. A finger crack to the left goes to a belay terrace, with easier ground and a short wall to the high point above.
Pull past the bulge to the side of the lower anchors, then stay with the crack all the way up.
Tiptoe over the slab to reach a hand-size crack roughly fifty feet off the deck. Plugging a cam there is optional; some leaders skip it and go for the anchors.
Boulder through the steep pockets to a ledge, then keep fighting your way along the overhanging wall above, clipping bolt after bolt until the anchors.
Clip the bolt shared with the neighbour and power through that start to a ledge. Veer right from there and keep battling along the overhanging wall.
